statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 13% after the 18:00 UTC Beige Book published into an unchanged range: NQ trades 29,149.50 inside a 28,927.25 to 29,213.00 day range, NDX cash is 29,122.34 below its 29,165.62 high, and VIX has slipped to a new session low of 15.24 against a 16.82 high. Stress eases to 58% with the 10-year flat at 4.794% and the 2-year easing after the release, but stays elevated on WTI at $91.15, the Strait of Hormuz backdrop and the after-close Broadcom report.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, reflecting observed two-way price discovery and decaying implied volatility rather than any resolution of the macro backdrop. Tail remains below the block threshold for most of the next 24 hours; forecast Tail crosses it only inside the narrow 20:00-23:00 UTC window covering the Broadcom results, the 21:00 UTC management call inside the CME maintenance halt and the 22:00 UTC futures reopen. Watch-band checkpoints sit in the final cash hour and across the Thursday 12:00-15:00 UTC block containing jobless claims, the US cash open and ISM Services. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 absorbs the Beige Book inside its range as VIX sets a new session low of 15.24
body:
The 18:00 UTC Beige Book has published and the price path did not change character. NQ futures trade 29,149.50, up 24.00 points or 0.08% from the 29,125.50 previous close, still inside the 28,927.25 to 29,213.00 day range on Yahoo Finance. The cash Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,122.34, up 45.12 points or 0.16%, against a 28,971.90 to 29,165.62 range. Neither session extreme has been challenged in the hour around the release, which is the direct opposite of the repeated extension after failed pullbacks that this Tail score measures. Tail steps down again from 14% to 13%.

The Beige Book itself described economic activity increasing modestly since early July, employment rising very slightly with five districts reporting no change, and prices increasing moderately in eight districts, alongside heightened contact uncertainty over energy prices, policy and international conflict. Reported market reaction was orderly: the S&P 500 held a gain of roughly 0.47% and the Nasdaq roughly 0.37%, with the 2-year yield easing about one basis point and the 10-year steady near 4.80%.

Cross-asset evidence supports the same reading. VIX is 15.24, down 6.73%, printing a new session low of 15.23 against a 16.82 high, so implied volatility is decaying rather than building. The 10-year sits at 4.794%, essentially unchanged inside a 4.768 to 4.806 range, with the most recent H.15 constant-maturity readings at 4.75% for the 10-year and 4.34% for the 2-year. Crude remains the firm factor: WTI trades $91.15, up 1.02%, with Brent at $95.67, holding this week's Strait of Hormuz risk premium. Delayed cross-asset context shows a split megacap tape, with NVDA and META firm against MSFT and TSLA lower, and software weaker than semiconductors. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction rather than amplifying a one-way path.

Mapped policy state is EA_ON. The narrow danger window is unchanged at 20:00 to 23:00 UTC, covering the Broadcom results after the 20:00 UTC cash close, the 21:00 UTC management call that runs inside the CME maintenance halt, and the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen where a single-step gap is most credible. Consensus looks for roughly $29.4 billion of revenue and about $16 billion of AI semiconductor revenue, and the stock fell about 13% after its previous report despite a beat, so guidance rather than the headline print is the swing variable. Watch-band checkpoints then sit across the Thursday block containing jobless claims at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC, two days before the August payrolls report.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment moved from the orange band during Tuesday's yield-and-oil driven selloff, through a long stretch of watch-band event/whipsaw readings overnight, into the green band from 12:00 UTC as the US session produced an orderly two-way recovery. Tail has fallen from 25% at 19:00 UTC yesterday to 14% at the 17:00 UTC assessment, with Stress easing from 77% to 60% over the same span. Three hours are marked unavailable: 20:00 and 01:00 UTC, where no assessment was published, and 16:00 UTC, where the scheduled run produced no snapshot.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are shaped by one concentrated corporate catalyst and one macro block. Forecast Tail stays in the low band for the current hour, steps into the watch band for the final cash hour, then crosses the block threshold across 20:00 to 23:00 UTC for the Broadcom release, the management call inside the futures maintenance halt and the 22:00 UTC reopen. Overnight the conditional path returns to the low band through the Asian and European sessions, before a second watch-band block on Thursday covering jobless claims and Fed Waller at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC US cash open and ISM Services at 14:00 UTC. Stress remains in the elevated band throughout on firm crude, a 10-year near multi-year highs and Friday's payroll print ahead of the September policy meeting.
